BidModifiersServiceBidModifierTerm.description:
A bid adjustment term is composed of 1 or more of the below dimensions, and a bid adjustment.
 A minimum of 1 dimension must be set, and there is no maximum on the number of dimensions. The same
 dimension (e.g., appId) cannot be used twice. If you have multiple dimension values, please provide
 them in the list, separated by commas.

 A bid adjustment term is evaluated by attempting to match dimension
 values with impression data. The bid adjustment is only applied if all dimensions in the bid adjustment term match,
 where matching is defined as: the dimension contains a dimension value in common with the impression data. However, if
 the "negative" field is set to true, then the bid adjustment will only be applied if no dimensions in the bid adjustment
 match. If one or more dimensions have a value in common with the impression data and the "negative" field is true,
 then the bid adjustment will not be applied.

 Please note that all the dimension values provided for dimensions are case-insensitive for matching purposes,
 except dimensions which use numeric values/IDs.
 These numeric value/ID related dimensions are:
 [behavioralSegment, creativeId, dayOfWeekUserTimezone, dayOfWeekUtc, hourOfWeekUserTimezone, hourOfWeekUtc].

adFormat.description: Valid values: "DISPLAY", "AUDIO", "VIDEO". Values are case insensitive.

appId.description: Application identifiers unique to the app and independent of the exchange. On Android, this should be a bundle or package name (e.g.,com.foo.mygame). On iOS, it is typically a numeric ID. Values are case sensitive.

appName.description: The name of the application from the App Store. Examples include: "Wordscapes", "Pinterest", "Yahoo Weather".

behavioralSegment.description: Unique identifier for Amazon audiences. Selection of segments in Audience for the adgroup is required in order to use them in bid adjustments. Example: 407259404244917362.

bidAdjustment.description:
The value used to upscale/downscale the Amazon DSP computed bid amount. This will be multiplied with the bid amount
 computed by Amazon DSP to derive the final bid amount. Please note that values will be truncated to 2 decimal places.
 If there are multiple term objects in a bid adjustment rule,
 then each bid adjustment will be multipled together to determine the total bid adjustment amount, which will
 be mulitplied with the Amazon DSP computed bid amount.

browser.description: The browser family of the user viewing the page. Example: "Chrome", "Mozilla", "Safari", "Firefox". Values are case insensitive.

city.description: Full name of the city. Values are case insensitive. Only listed values are allowed.

country.description: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, based on the IP address of the user. Example: "JP". Values are case insensitive.

deviceMake.description: The make of the device. Example: "APPLE", "GOOGLE", "SAMSUNG", "AMAZON". Values are case insensitive.

deviceType.description: The device type of the user viewing the ad. Valid Values: "Phone", "Tablet", "PC", "TV", "ConnectedDevice", "SetTopBox". Values are case insensitive.

dma.description: Designated market area. Example: "DMA501" would be used for Nielsen DMA corresponding to New York, NY. Values are case insensitive.

domain.description: Domain of a site. Example: "msn.com" Values are case insensitive.

negative.description:
Determines when the bidAdjustment is applied. Defaults to false. If specified as true, then it defines a
     matched term as the scenario when the impression data has no matches with the specified dimensions (exactly zero) and will
     only apply the bidAdjustment in this case.

operatingSystem.description: The operating system of the user viewing the page. Example: "MacOS", "Windows", "iOS", "Android", "Fire OS". Values are case insensitive.

postalCode.description: The postal code with 2-letter country code prefix, based on the IP address of the user. Use '-' as a separator between country code and postal code. Example: BR-03012, US-90210, MX-16900, JP-100-0004. Values are case insensitive.

region.description: The geographical state, based on the IP address of the user. Values are case insensitive.

slotPosition.description: Whether the slot is above, or below the fold. Valid Values: "ABOVE", "BELOW", "UNKNOWN". Values are case insensitive.

slotSize.description: The slot's pixel size for the ad. This functions the same as the creative size with our slot-creative matching process. Example: 300x50.

termId.description: A system generated identifier for the term starting from 1.

Returns a list of active bid adjustment rule(s) belonging to the specified Ads AccountId. You can use a single adGroupId in request body to return a list of active bid adjustment rule(s) filtered by an associated adgroup. Alternatively, you can use a list of adGroupIds in request body to return a list of active bid adjustment rule(s) filtered by the list of adGroups. The response will return association status of the adGroupIds to the bid adjustment rule(s).To view all past bid adjustment associations,set active flag to false. Use includeRuleExpression to control whether rule expressions are included in the response.

DSP Rodeo Entity ID, DSP Advertiser Account ID

**Parameter name**:
Amazon-Ads-AccountId

header

put.description:
Associates a bid adjustment rule with an adgroup. Association requests are fulfilled immediately,
however it can take ~1 hour for the association to take place in the ADSP bidding system. If a prior association for
the adGroup exists, it will be overridden with a new association. You can use the ListBidModifierRules that returns a
list of bid adjustment rule(s) filtered by associated adgroups to check if the adGroup already has a bid modifier associated with.

**Authorized resource type**:
DSP Rodeo Entity ID, DSP Advertiser Account ID

**Parameter name**:
Amazon-Ads-AccountId

**Parameter in**:
header

**Requires one of these permissions**:
["campaign_edit"]
